newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms offshore, interbank steady late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms offshore, interbank steady late.

text.p: The Thai baht rose further against the dollar late in the offshore market as offshore players facing a severe shortage of baht continued to sell the U.S. unit, dealers said.
In the offshore market, the baht rose to 24.670/24.770 to the dollar in late trade from 24.900/25.100 early.
"Foreigners are still selling dollars offshore to cover baht positions," said one local dealer.
In the onshore market, the baht was traded lower to 25.860/25.880 late compared with 25.840/25.870 early as local banks bought to cover short dollar positions, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.84 per dollar on Tuesday versus 25.81 on Monday.

The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 140/160 satangs per dollar late in the offshore market against 100/150 in the morning. In domestic market, the one-month swap premium was at 20/30 satangs versus 25/35 in the morning.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 15.00/16.00 percent, unchanged from early morning trade as liquidity remained tight, dealers said.
The heavy dollar buying in the foreign exchange market and withdrawal of corporate tax payments from the system reduced money supply in the market, dealers said.
Banks also maintained their own funds to meet the central bank's reserve requirements due on the seventh and 22nd of every month, dealers said.
